proposals.relationship: Wood challenges Tuchman’s March of Folly for hindsight, anachronistic standards and overly narrow explanations, while praising parts of its narrative.
proposals.evidence_note: The complete 1984 review reconstructs Tuchman’s contemporary-warning criteria before arguing that unpredictable outcomes make folly versus determination retrospectively unstable; Wood disputes the top-down Reformation and American Revolution accounts. He praises the Vietnam chapter while noting its thin account of opponents. This is Wood’s particular criticism, not a certified refutation, dismissal of all popular narrative, or repetition of Stone’s 1978 Mirror objection. Tuchman’s publisher opening explicitly requires contemporary recognition and alternatives; that intent remains alongside Wood’s objection.
